# Adjudication Task — Chapter 395

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃395화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|「따라와.」
  6|
  7|매직 존슨이 우리를 이끌고 향한 곳은 다름 아닌 병원 옥상이었다.
  8|
  9|헬기도, 제트기도 보이지 않는 텅 빈 착륙장을 훑어본 내가 물었다.
 10|
 11|“아무것도 없는데요?”
 12|
 13|「아니지. 내가 있잖아.」
 14|
 15|매직 존슨의 대답은 짧고 간결했지만, 그 말에 담긴 의미는 결코 간단한 것이 아니었다.
 16|
 17|나와 같은 생각을 했는지, 최 팀장의 눈이 살짝 커진다.
 18|
 19|“미스터 존슨. 혹시?”
 20|
 21|「그래, 우린 텔레포트(Teleporte) 마법으로 이동할 거야.」
 22|
 23|텔레포트. 쉽게 말해서 순간이동.
 24|
 25|매직 존슨은 마치 세발자전거를 타자는 듯이 편안하게 얘기했지만, 텔레포트 마법이 극악한 난이도로 악명이 높다는 건 익히 알려진 사실이었다.
 26|
 27|마법 발현을 위해 충족시켜야 하는 까다로운 조건들은 둘째 치고, 까딱 좌표라도 어긋나는 날에는 골로 가기 쉬웠다.
 28|
 29|단 한 걸음 차이로 사과나무나 바위와 한 몸이 될 수도 있다니, 끔찍한 일이지.
 30|
 31|“……그냥 제트기 타고 가면 안 될까요?”
 32|
 33|「놉.」
 34|
 35|단호하게 대답한 매직 존슨이 눈을 가늘게 떴다.
 36|
 37|「헤이, 진. 설마 지금 나를 못 믿는 건 아니겠지? 나 매직 존슨이야. 직접 보여 줘야 믿겠어?」
 38|
 39|“…….”
 40|
 41|당신이 그런 말 하니까 더 이상하게 들리잖아.
 42|
 43|그가 보여 주려는 게 텔레포트 마법이건 존슨이건 상관없다. 나는 그저 제트기를 타고 평화롭게 이동하고 싶을 뿐이다.
 44|
 45|내 간절한 눈빛을 알아챈 최 팀장이 입을 열었다.
 46|
 47|“미스터 존슨. 아시겠지만 이곳은 아크 리치의 힘이 닿는 곳입니다. 마법 방해는 물론이고 통신도 원활하지 않아요.”
 48|
 49|「아, 그거였군. 난 또 뭐라고.」
 50|
 51|매직 존슨이 피식 웃었다.
 52|
 53|「두 사람은 내가 여기에 어떻게 왔다고 생각해?」
 54|
 55|“어?”
 56|
 57|“설마?”
 58|
 59|「맞아. 텔레포트로 왔어. 약간 거슬리기는 했지만, 이 매직 존슨을 묶어 둘 수는 없지.」
 60|
 61|딱!
 62|
 63|매직 존슨이 손가락을 튕기자 허공에서 불기둥이 솟구친다. 숨 쉬듯 자연스러운 마법의 발현. 지금까지 마력 방해 때문에 제대로 마법을 사용할 수 없었던 공안 무력부의 마법사들과는 대조적인 모습이다.
 64|
 65|“처음부터 가능했던 겁니까?”
 66|
 67|「당연히 아니지. 지금까지 마력 방해가 있어도 어지간한 마법은 그럭저럭 쓸 수 있었는데, 텔레포트 같은 마법은 너무 위험해서 시도해 볼 엄두도 안 나더라고.」
 68|
 69|“그럼…….”
 70|
 71|「아크 리치. 놈의 힘이 아주 조금씩 줄어들고 있었어. 특히 어젯밤을 기점으로 방해 요소가 상당 부분 사라지게 되었지. 뭐, 아직도 통신 상태는 개판인 것 같지만.」
 72|
 73|전 세계를 통틀어 셋밖에 없다는 대마법사이기에 할 수 있는 소리고, 가능한 일이다.
 74|
 75|흰 이빨을 드러내며 웃어 보인 매직 존슨이 우리를 향해 손을 내밀었다.
 76|
 77|「이 정도면 나를 믿기에는 충분한 것 같은데. 안 그래?」
 78|
 79|“그러시다면야, 뭐.”
 80|
 81|별다른 망설임 없이 손을 맞잡은 나와 달리, 최 팀장은 조용히 뒤로 물러났다.
 82|
 83|“최 팀장님?”
 84|
 85|“전 남겠습니다.”
 86|
 87|「왜 그래, 최?」
 88|
 89|“아직 처리해야 할 일이 있어서요. 어차피 발언권이 미비한 저로서는 가서 들으나, 전해 들으나 매한가지입니다.”
 90|
 91|최 팀장은 언제나 냉정하게 상황을 바라본다. 스스로 흐름을 바꿀 수 없다면, 후 순위의 일을 끌어당겨 해결한다.
 92|
 93|나는 잘못된 생각이라 말해 주고 싶었지만 잠자코 고개를 끄덕였다.
 94|
 95|‘틀린 말은 아니니까.’
 96|
 97|발언권이 강한 S급 헌터들 역시 결국은 대부분이 타국의 용병이며 빌려온 칼일 뿐이다.
 98|
 99|그렇기에 샤오 양 주석이나 웨이펑후 국방부장도 전체 지휘권은 자신들에게 있음을 분명히 못 박았었다.
100|
101|「최가 빠지다니! 이럴 수는 없어! 진은 매력이 없다고!」
102|
103|“…….”
104|
105|진짜 못 박아 버리고 싶네. 아니, 한편으로는 다행인가?
106|
107|한참을 징징거리던 매직 존슨은 아쉬움 가득한 얼굴로 최 팀장에게 작별 인사를 건넸다.
108|
109|「어쩔 수 없지. 그럼 다음에 봐, 최.」
110|
111|“살펴 가십시오.”
112|
113|「살펴 가긴 뭘. 어차피 한순간인데.」
114|
115|어깨를 으쓱해 보인 매직 존슨이 내게 물었다.
116|
117|「헤이, 진. 준비됐어?」
118|
119|“네.”
120|
121|「내 손 꽉 잡아. 놓치지 않게.」
122|
123|“……깍지는 왜 끼세요. 그냥 손바닥만 잡으면 안 돼요?”
124|
125|이런 건 연인들끼리나 하는 거 아닌가.
126|
127|이십 대 후반의 모태솔로인 나로서는 거구의 흑인과 깍지 손을 낀다는 게 불편할 수밖에 없었다.
128|
129|떨떠름해하는 내게 매직 존슨이 상냥한 어조로 말했다.
130|
131|「원한다면 풀어도 좋아. 그런데 이동 중에 손을 놓치면 죽을 수도 있어.」
132|
133|나는 어렸을 적 첫사랑을 떠올리며 매직 존슨의 손을 단단히 붙잡았다.
134|
135|“갑시다, 달링.”
136|
137|매직 존슨이 정색하며 대답했다.
138|
139|「미안한데 진은 내 취향 아니야. 그 정도로 세게 잡을 필요는 없으니까 힘 좀 풀어 줄래?」
140|
141|“……아, 예.”
142|
143|「그럼, 간다?」
144|
145|입을 열어 대답하려던 그때.
146|
147|쏴아아아악!
148|
149|‘흡!’
150|
151|숨이 턱 막히고 팽팽한 공기가 전신을 조여 왔다.
152|
153|흐릿해지는 시야 속에서 최 팀장의 모습이 신기루처럼 일렁이더니 이내 사라진다.
154|
155|뒤집히는 땅과 하늘, 그리고 마침내 찾아온 엄청난 해방감.
156|
157|“푸하!”
158|
159|참았던 숨을 토해 낸 나는 깊이 숨을 들이마셨다. 폐부 깊숙이 스며드는 시원한 공기. 눈을 깜빡이자 잠시 흐릿했던 시야가 또렷해진다.
160|
161|체감상으로는 1초 남짓한 시간이 흘렀을 뿐인데, 전혀 다른 풍경과 사람들이 그곳에 있었다.
162|
163|「마지막 손님이 오셨군.」
164|
165|중앙 군사위원회 국방부장 웨이펑후, 일주일 사이 십 년은 늙어 버린 듯한 그가 다가와 내 어깨를 두드렸다.
166|
167|「모두 기다리고 있소. 함께 들어갑시다.」
168|
169|“자, 잠깐만요.”
170|
171|「응?」
172|
173|“다가오지…… 우웨에에에에엑!”
174|
175|촤아아악!
176|
177|참고로 나는 키가 큰 편이다. 웨이펑후보다 머리 두 개 정도.
178|
179|듬성듬성한 노장군의 정수리를 향해 토사물을 쏟아 내는 내게, 매직 존슨의 목소리가 들려왔다.
180|
181|「아, 멀미 증상이 심해진다는 걸 말 안 해 줬구나. 미안해, 진. 미안해요, 웨이펑후.」
182|
183|“그런 건 진작 말해 줬어야, 우웨에에엑!”
184|
185|「……하.」
186|
187|회의에 참석하기까지는 아주 약간의 시간이 추가로 소요되었다.
188|
189|
190|
191|* * *
192|
193|
194|
195|커다란 대회의실. 어두컴컴한 그곳에서는 홀로그램 영상이 흘러나오는 중이었다.
196|
197|한 사람의 시선이 고스란히 담긴 영상에 복잡한 조종간과 강화유리 밖으로 흩어지는 구름이 담긴다. 하강과 동시에 보이기 시작하는 까마득한 점들도.
198|
199|지상을 메운 그것들은 오와 열도 없이 파도처럼 밀려드는 중이었다.
200|
201|‘몬스터.’
202|
203|나는 이 시선의 주인이 전투기 파일럿이라는 사실을 어렵지 않게 알 수 있었다. 헤드캠을 착용한 그가 어딘가로 무전을 보냈다.
204|
205|- 여기는 YANU-4885. 반복한다. YANU-4885. 목표 확인. 조준 완료.
206|
207|- 사격을 허가한다.
208|
209|치직, 치지직.
210|
211|노이즈 낀 무전이었지만 알아듣기에는 무리가 없었다. 깊이 심호흡한 파일럿을 망설이지 않고 임무를 수행했다.
212|
213|구궁.
214|
215|작은 흔들림과 함께 전투기에 탑재되어 있던 미사일이 쏘아졌다. 순식간에 하나의 점이 되어 쏘아진 그것이 진군하는 몬스터 군단의 중심에 작렬하려던 그 순간.
216|
217|쏴아아악.
218|
219|놈들의 머리 위, 텅 빈 허공에서 난데없이 나타난 검은 소용돌이가 미사일을 집어삼켰다.
220|
221|- 흐읍!
222|
223|파일럿이 다급함이 느껴지는 헛숨과 함께 조종간의 붉은색 버튼을 눌렀다. 하지만…….
224|
225|콰앙! 치지직.
226|
227|갑자기 들이닥친 굉음과 함께 영상은 끊겼다. 홀로그램이 사라지고, 웨이펑후 국방부장이 무거운 표정으로 입을 열었다.
228|
229|「다른 분들은 어떻게 보시오?」
230|
231|매직 존슨이 시가에 불을 붙이며 대답했다.
232|
233|「텔레포트 마법이군요. 발사된 미사일을 기체 위로 이동시켰어요.」
234|
235|「미스터 존슨. 당신이라면 가능하오?」
236|
237|곰곰이 생각에 잠겨 있던 그가 입을 뗐다.
238|
239|「어렵지 않죠. 하지만 저 정도로 신속하고 정확하게 할 자신은 없습니다.」
240|
241|「대마법사인 당신이라 해도 말이오?」
242|
243|「……음.」
244|
245|살짝 고개를 끄덕인 매직 존슨이 시가 연기를 내뿜었다.
246|
247|그 역시 역사에 남을 전공을 세운 S급 헌터. 그만큼 자신의 실력에 자부심이 있었을 테니, 아크 리치라는 몬스터에게 뒤진다는 사실이 마음에 들지는 않을 것이다.
248|
249|하지만 이 자리는 자존심을 위해 마련된 자리가 아니다. 현실을 직시해야 한다.
250|
251|「그럼 화력 지원은 기대하기 어렵게 됐네. 큰 거 한 방 잘못 쐈다가는 대참사가 벌어질 테니까.」
252|
253|파이 첸이 가느다란 손가락으로 술잔을 건드리며 말을 이었다.
254|
255|「어느 정도 예상은 했지만…… 이렇게 된 이상 지상에서 결판을 내는 수밖에.」
256|
257|「지금대로라면 전황은 차차 나아질 것이다. 본 왕자가 이끄는 대영제국의 왕실 근위대가 몬스터 군단을 박살 냈으니까. 그보다 지금 그대가 마시고 있는 술, 혹시 로마네콩티 45년 산인지?」
258|
259|「아닌데.」
260|
261|「흠. 마실 줄 모르는군.」
262|
263|필릭스 왕자의 말에 파이 첸이 눈을 치켜떴다.
264|
265|「어머, 이 어린애가 뭐라는 거야. 얘, 정신 좀 차려. 대영제국은 오래전에 해체됐고 몬스터들이 물러난 건 너희가 몇 번 승리해서가 아냐. 네 맞은편에 있는 저 녀석 덕분이지.」
266|
267|필릭스 왕자가 힐끗 나를 바라봤다.
268|
269|「서부 전선에서 큰 공을 세웠다는 이야기는 들었네만…… 진정 그 말들이 모두 사실인가?」
270|
271|내가 거짓말이라도 친다는 거야, 뭐야.
272|
273|나는 어이없는 표정으로 필릭스 왕자를 바라보았다.
274|
275|“그럼 사실이지, 구라겠냐? 믿기 싫으면 믿지 마.”
276|
277|「그토록 큰 공을 세운 것은 칭찬해 줄 만하지만, 언행이 상당히 불손하군. 필릭스 전하라고 지칭하고, 항상 경어를 쓰도록.」
278|
279|나는 선선히 그 요구를 들어주었다.
280|
281|“전하, 혹시 피쉬 앤 칩스를 잘못 쳐 드셨습니까?”
282|
283|「으음. 용맹무쌍하나 무례하기 짝이 없는 자로군.」
284|
285|“…….”
286|
287|무례하기 짝이 없기는 개뿔이. 불알 한 짝을 없애 버릴까 보다.
288|
289|참고로 일주일 전쯤에 한 번 털렸던 놈은 입을 꾹 다물고 눈도 마주치려 하지 않는다.
290|
291|‘조용해지니까 좋긴 한데 뭔가 찝찝하단 말이지.’
292|

[P39]
“Well, if you put it that way.”

[P40]
I took his hand without much hesitation, but Team Leader Choi quietly stepped back.

[P41]
“Team Leader Choi?”

[P42]
“I’ll stay here.”

[P43]
“Why, Choi?”

[P44]
“There are still matters I need to handle. Besides, given how little influence I have in the discussion, attending in person or hearing about it afterward will make little difference.”

[P45]
Team Leader Choi always assessed the situation coolly. If he couldn’t change the course of events himself, he pulled lower-priority work forward and dealt with that instead.

[P46]
I wanted to tell him he was mistaken, but I merely nodded.

[P47]
*He wasn’t wrong.*

[P48]
Even the S-rank Hunters whose opinions carried weight were ultimately mercenaries from other countries—borrowed blades.

[P49]
That was why Chairman Shao Yang and Minister Wei Fenghu had made it clear that overall command remained in their hands.

[P50]
“Choi’s not coming? This can’t be happening! Jin has no Charm!”

[P51]
“……”

[P52]
*I really want to drive a nail through him. Then again, maybe this is for the best.*

[P53]
After whining for quite some time, Magic Johnson reluctantly said goodbye to Team Leader Choi.

[P54]
“Can’t be helped. See you next time, Choi.”

[P55]
“Take care.”

[P56]
“Take care of what? It’ll be over in an instant.”

[P57]
Magic Johnson shrugged and turned to me.

[P58]
“Hey, Jin. Ready?”

[P59]
“Yes.”

[P60]
“Hold my hand tight. Don’t let go.”

[P61]
“……Why are you interlocking our fingers? Can’t we just hold hands normally?”

[P62]
*Isn’t this the sort of thing couples do?*

[P63]
As a guy in his late twenties who had been single his entire life, I couldn’t help feeling uncomfortable about interlocking fingers with a huge Black man.

[P64]
Magic Johnson spoke gently when he saw my reluctance.

[P65]
“You can let go if you want. But if you lose your grip during the journey, you might die.”

[P66]
Thinking of my first love from childhood, I clutched Magic Johnson’s hand tightly.

[P67]
“Let’s go, darling.”

[P68]
Magic Johnson’s expression turned stern.

[P69]
“Sorry, but you’re not my type, Jin. You don’t have to squeeze that hard, so could you ease up?”

[P70]
“……Oh. Right.”

[P71]
“Then, here we go.”

[P72]
I opened my mouth to answer—

[P73]
Whoooooosh!

[P74]
*Hngh!*

[P75]
My breath caught, and the taut air constricted around my entire body.

[P76]
Through my blurring vision, Team Leader Choi wavered like a mirage before vanishing.

[P77]
The earth and sky flipped upside down.

[P78]
Then, at last, came an overwhelming sense of release.

[P79]
“Hah!”

[P80]
I expelled the breath I had been holding and inhaled deeply. Cool air filled my lungs. I blinked, and my briefly clouded vision cleared.

[P81]
It felt as though barely a second had passed, yet an entirely different landscape and different people now surrounded me.

[P82]
“Our final guest has arrived.”

[P83]
Wei Fenghu, Minister of National Defense under China’s Central Military Commission, approached and patted me on the shoulder. He looked as though he had aged ten years in the past week.

[P84]
“Everyone is waiting. Let us go inside together.”

[P85]
“W-wait.”

[P86]
“Yes?”

[P87]
“Don’t come any closer…”

[P88]
“Uweeeeeegh!”

[P89]
Splash!

[P90]
For the record, I’m fairly tall. About two heads taller than Wei Fenghu.

[P91]
As I emptied my stomach over the thinning crown of the old general’s head, Magic Johnson’s voice reached me.

[P92]
“Ah, I forgot to mention that teleportation makes motion sickness worse. Sorry, Jin. Sorry, Wei Fenghu.”

[P93]
“You should’ve told me that sooner—uweeeeeegh!”

[P94]
“……Hah.”

[P95]
It took a little longer than expected for me to join the meeting.

[P96]
* * *

[P97]
A holographic recording played in the darkness of a vast conference room.

[P98]
The footage showed exactly what one person had seen: a complicated control panel, clouds scattering beyond reinforced glass, and tiny specks appearing far below as the aircraft descended.

[P99]
The things covering the ground surged forward like waves, with no ranks or formation.

[P100]
*Monsters.*

[P101]
It wasn’t difficult to tell that the footage came from a fighter pilot’s perspective. Wearing a head-mounted camera, the pilot radioed someone.

[P102]
—This is YANU-4885. I repeat, YANU-4885. Target confirmed. Locked on.

[P103]
—You are cleared to fire.

[P104]
Crackle. Crackle.

[P105]
The transmission was riddled with static, but the words were clear enough. The pilot took a deep breath and carried out the mission without hesitation.

[P106]
Rumble.

[P107]
The fighter trembled slightly as one of its missiles launched. It dwindled into a speck as it streaked toward the center of the advancing monster army—

[P108]
Whoosh!

[P109]
A black vortex abruptly appeared in the empty air above the monsters and swallowed the missile.

[P110]
—Hngh!

[P111]
The pilot gasped and hurriedly pressed a red button on the control panel.

[P112]
But then—

[P113]
Boom! Crackle.

[P114]
A deafening explosion erupted, and the footage cut out.

[P115]
The hologram vanished. Minister Wei Fenghu surveyed the room with a grave expression.

[P116]
“What do the rest of you make of it?”

[P117]
Magic Johnson lit a cigar before answering.

[P118]
“Teleportation magic. The missile was transported above the fighter.”

[P119]
“Mr. Johnson, could you do the same?”

[P120]
After a moment of thought, Magic Johnson answered.

[P121]
“It wouldn’t be difficult. But I’m not confident I could do it that quickly or accurately.”

[P122]
“Even for an archmage such as yourself?”

[P123]
“……Hmm.”

[P124]
Magic Johnson gave a slight nod and exhaled cigar smoke.

[P125]
He, too, was an S-rank Hunter whose accomplishments would go down in history. He took pride in his abilities, so admitting that a monster like the Arch Lich had surpassed him couldn’t have been pleasant.

[P126]
But this meeting wasn’t about protecting anyone’s pride.

[P127]
We had to face reality.

[P128]
“Then we can’t count on fire support. If we launch anything too powerful and it gets redirected, the result could be catastrophic.”

[P129]
Faye Chen ran one slender finger along her wineglass as she continued.

[P130]
“I expected as much, but now that it’s come to this, we have no choice but to settle the matter on the ground.”

[P131]
“If matters continue as they are, the tide of battle will gradually improve. The royal guard of the British Empire, led by this prince, has crushed the monster army. More importantly, that wine you are drinking—is it perhaps a 1945 Romanée-Conti?”

[P132]
“No.”

[P133]
“Hm. You don’t know how to drink.”

[P134]
Faye Chen glared at Prince Felix.

[P135]
“Oh, my. What is this child talking about? Get a grip. The British Empire was dissolved long ago, and the monsters didn’t retreat because you won a few battles. They retreated because of that fellow sitting across from you.”

[P136]
Prince Felix glanced at me.

[P137]
“I heard that you distinguished yourself greatly on the western front…but are all those stories truly accurate?”

[P138]
*What, does he think I’m lying?*

[P139]
I stared at Prince Felix incredulously.

[P140]
“Of course they’re true. You think I made it all up? If you don’t want to believe me, don’t.”

[P141]
“Your great achievements may be worthy of praise, but your words and conduct are remarkably insolent. You will refer to me as His Highness and always speak respectfully.”

[P142]
I readily complied with his demand.

[P143]
“Your Highness, did you choke on your fish and chips?”

[P144]
“Hmm. A man of matchless courage, yet utterly lacking in manners.”

[P145]
“……”

[P146]
*Utterly lacking in manners, my ass. Maybe I should make sure he’s lacking one ball, too.*

[P147]
For the record, the guy I’d beaten up about a week ago kept his mouth firmly shut and wouldn’t even meet my eyes.

[P148]
*It’s nice that he’s quiet, but something about it feels off.*

[P149]
Given Wu Heixing’s stupidity, I’d expected him to come at me at least a few more times. Either he was more cowardly than I’d thought, or I had misjudged him.

[P150]
More importantly, someone else in the room bothered me far more than Wu Heixing did.

[P151]
“You’ve been awfully quiet. Don’t you have anything to say?”

[P152]
Lee Jungryong—the snake coiled in wait—smiled gently.

[P153]
“Thank you for your concern, but I’m fine. A mercenary’s virtue lies in following his employer’s wishes without complaint.”

[P154]
“Oh, is that so?”

[P155]
“It’s a simple principle.”

[P156]
I smiled back.

[P157]
“But for someone who says that, your performance has been a little lackluster. Things on the northern front don’t seem to be going very well. Was that your employer’s wish too?”

[P158]
“……!”

[P159]
At my words, silence descended over the room as if everyone had been doused with cold water.

[P160]
As every gaze turned toward him, Lee Jungryong stroked his chin.

[P161]
“I find that remark unpleasant. Ares Guild and I did our best.”

[P162]
“Your best? Really?”

[P163]
“We fought ten battles over the past week and won nine of them. Although we unfortunately suffered one defeat, I would call that an impressive military record.”

[P164]
Ten battles, nine victories, one defeat.

[P165]
By the numbers, it certainly looked impressive.

[P166]
But two days ago, when Team Leader Choi and I heard about the defeat on the northern front, we had both let out hollow laughs.

[P167]
*What a sly old man.*

[P168]
Lee Jungryong was one of the strongest men in the world—or, even by Murim standards, an incredibly powerful martial artist.

[P169]
Given his personality, there was no chance he had revealed the full extent of his abilities. He had to be even stronger than the public believed.

[P170]
And someone like that had the nerve to say—

[P171]
*“Unfortunately suffered one defeat,” my ass.*

[P172]
I couldn’t speak for anyone else, but I was certain.

[P173]
If Lee Jungryong had taken the field and still lost, then the defeat had been intentional from beginning to end.

[P174]
The members of Ares Guild had withdrawn intact despite the staggering casualties around them. They were living proof.

[P175]
*Though since I can’t prove anything, I suppose it’s still only a suspicion.*

[P176]
That was also why Lee Jungryong could remain so relaxed. He loosely crossed his arms.

[P177]
“I regret the defeat that day, but I would appreciate it if you refrained from making hasty accusations. There was a clear reason for our loss.”

[P178]
“A clear reason?”

[P179]
“Who could have expected a Death Knight to appear under those circumstances? Once the commander died, the ensuing confusion became impossible to control.”

[P180]
“A Death Knight…”

[P181]
“I heard they appeared on the western front last night as well. Is that not so?”

[P182]
His words brought something to mind.

[P183]
The testimony of the civilian couple rescued from the small city.

[P184]
Ten Death Knights had slaughtered nearly a thousand troops, while their leader, the black knight, had left without killing the couple for some unknown reason.

[P185]
That black knight had bothered me ever since I heard their story.

[P186]
“Then among the ones that appeared on the northern front, was there perhaps—”

[P187]
My question to Lee Jungryong never reached its end.

[P188]
Urgent footsteps raced down the corridor, and someone who looked like a Chinese officer burst through the door.

[P189]
Bang!

[P190]
“Huff, huff. Emergency! This is an emergency!”

[P191]
He struggled to catch his breath before continuing.

[P192]
“We’ve received word that the monster armies are advancing! Fighting has broken out on every front!”

[P193]
“……What?”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 395

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃395화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|「따라와.」
  6|
  7|매직 존슨이 우리를 이끌고 향한 곳은 다름 아닌 병원 옥상이었다.
  8|
  9|헬기도, 제트기도 보이지 않는 텅 빈 착륙장을 훑어본 내가 물었다.
 10|
 11|“아무것도 없는데요?”
 12|
 13|「아니지. 내가 있잖아.」
 14|
 15|매직 존슨의 대답은 짧고 간결했지만, 그 말에 담긴 의미는 결코 간단한 것이 아니었다.
 16|
 17|나와 같은 생각을 했는지, 최 팀장의 눈이 살짝 커진다.
 18|
 19|“미스터 존슨. 혹시?”
 20|
 21|「그래, 우린 텔레포트(Teleporte) 마법으로 이동할 거야.」
 22|
 23|텔레포트. 쉽게 말해서 순간이동.
 24|
 25|매직 존슨은 마치 세발자전거를 타자는 듯이 편안하게 얘기했지만, 텔레포트 마법이 극악한 난이도로 악명이 높다는 건 익히 알려진 사실이었다.
 26|
 27|마법 발현을 위해 충족시켜야 하는 까다로운 조건들은 둘째 치고, 까딱 좌표라도 어긋나는 날에는 골로 가기 쉬웠다.
 28|
 29|단 한 걸음 차이로 사과나무나 바위와 한 몸이 될 수도 있다니, 끔찍한 일이지.
 30|
 31|“……그냥 제트기 타고 가면 안 될까요?”
 32|
 33|「놉.」
 34|
 35|단호하게 대답한 매직 존슨이 눈을 가늘게 떴다.
 36|
 37|「헤이, 진. 설마 지금 나를 못 믿는 건 아니겠지? 나 매직 존슨이야. 직접 보여 줘야 믿겠어?」
 38|
 39|“…….”
 40|
 41|당신이 그런 말 하니까 더 이상하게 들리잖아.
 42|
 43|그가 보여 주려는 게 텔레포트 마법이건 존슨이건 상관없다. 나는 그저 제트기를 타고 평화롭게 이동하고 싶을 뿐이다.
 44|
 45|내 간절한 눈빛을 알아챈 최 팀장이 입을 열었다.
 46|
 47|“미스터 존슨. 아시겠지만 이곳은 아크 리치의 힘이 닿는 곳입니다. 마법 방해는 물론이고 통신도 원활하지 않아요.”
 48|
 49|「아, 그거였군. 난 또 뭐라고.」
 50|
 51|매직 존슨이 피식 웃었다.
 52|
 53|「두 사람은 내가 여기에 어떻게 왔다고 생각해?」
 54|
 55|“어?”
 56|
 57|“설마?”
 58|
 59|「맞아. 텔레포트로 왔어. 약간 거슬리기는 했지만, 이 매직 존슨을 묶어 둘 수는 없지.」
 60|
 61|딱!
 62|
 63|매직 존슨이 손가락을 튕기자 허공에서 불기둥이 솟구친다. 숨 쉬듯 자연스러운 마법의 발현. 지금까지 마력 방해 때문에 제대로 마법을 사용할 수 없었던 공안 무력부의 마법사들과는 대조적인 모습이다.
 64|
 65|“처음부터 가능했던 겁니까?”
 66|
 67|「당연히 아니지. 지금까지 마력 방해가 있어도 어지간한 마법은 그럭저럭 쓸 수 있었는데, 텔레포트 같은 마법은 너무 위험해서 시도해 볼 엄두도 안 나더라고.」
 68|
 69|“그럼…….”
 70|
 71|「아크 리치. 놈의 힘이 아주 조금씩 줄어들고 있었어. 특히 어젯밤을 기점으로 방해 요소가 상당 부분 사라지게 되었지. 뭐, 아직도 통신 상태는 개판인 것 같지만.」
 72|
 73|전 세계를 통틀어 셋밖에 없다는 대마법사이기에 할 수 있는 소리고, 가능한 일이다.
 74|
 75|흰 이빨을 드러내며 웃어 보인 매직 존슨이 우리를 향해 손을 내밀었다.
 76|
 77|「이 정도면 나를 믿기에는 충분한 것 같은데. 안 그래?」
 78|
 79|“그러시다면야, 뭐.”
 80|
 81|별다른 망설임 없이 손을 맞잡은 나와 달리, 최 팀장은 조용히 뒤로 물러났다.
 82|
 83|“최 팀장님?”
 84|
 85|“전 남겠습니다.”
 86|
 87|「왜 그래, 최?」
 88|
 89|“아직 처리해야 할 일이 있어서요. 어차피 발언권이 미비한 저로서는 가서 들으나, 전해 들으나 매한가지입니다.”
 90|
 91|최 팀장은 언제나 냉정하게 상황을 바라본다. 스스로 흐름을 바꿀 수 없다면, 후 순위의 일을 끌어당겨 해결한다.
 92|
 93|나는 잘못된 생각이라 말해 주고 싶었지만 잠자코 고개를 끄덕였다.
 94|
 95|‘틀린 말은 아니니까.’
 96|
 97|발언권이 강한 S급 헌터들 역시 결국은 대부분이 타국의 용병이며 빌려온 칼일 뿐이다.
 98|
 99|그렇기에 샤오 양 주석이나 웨이펑후 국방부장도 전체 지휘권은 자신들에게 있음을 분명히 못 박았었다.
100|
101|「최가 빠지다니! 이럴 수는 없어! 진은 매력이 없다고!」
102|
103|“…….”
104|
105|진짜 못 박아 버리고 싶네. 아니, 한편으로는 다행인가?
106|
107|한참을 징징거리던 매직 존슨은 아쉬움 가득한 얼굴로 최 팀장에게 작별 인사를 건넸다.
108|
109|「어쩔 수 없지. 그럼 다음에 봐, 최.」
110|
111|“살펴 가십시오.”
112|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
